---
title: 'About the project'
subtitle: 'An atlas of curiosity, made one week at a time.'
---

52 Weeks of Maps is a personal mapping project by [tungufoss](https://github.com/tungufoss). The aim is to create and share a data-driven map every week during 2027, post it on LinkedIn, and keep a lasting record here.

The maps may explore research, Iceland, history, technology, board games, or an unexpected dataset. Each entry should make its sources and limitations clear and explain how the map was made.

## Open methods

The project uses Python for data preparation, a shared PostGIS database for spatial analysis, R for cartography, and Quarto for publication. Code and publishable assets live in [tungufoss/maps](https://github.com/tungufoss/maps).

The website reuses the shared website theme from [quarto-hi](https://github.com/tungufoss/quarto-hi): Jost typography, blue navigation and footer, turquoise accents, and its heading, table, code, and callout styles. The gallery layout adapts those patterns for this project. University logos are omitted.
